newsitem.title: UK: Newcastle say Dalglish underlines club's strength.
newsitem.headline: Newcastle say Dalglish underlines club's strength.

text.p: Newcastle United said on Thursday that their success in hiring Kenny Dalglish to manage the soccer team underlined the strength of the club as it prepares for a flotation in which it hopes to raise up to 50 million stg.
Dalglish, who has won the English league title as a manager with Liverpool and Blackburn Rovers, was appointed on Tuesday night, just days after Kevin Keegan's shock resignation.
"The past few days have been hectic but we have come out of it positively as we have managed to deliver the goods," Newcastle's joint chief executive Mark Corbidge told Reuters.
Corbidge again denied that bankers NatWest Markets had hastened Keegan's departure by insisting that he leave immediately if he was serious about threats to quit.
"The board runs the business. If we get into the game of trying to second guess the City then we show a weakness of management which the City would not welcome," Corbidge said.
Looking ahead to the spring flotation, Corbidge said "we think we have a strong story to sell as one of the leading soccer businesses".
He said that no specific sum from the flotation had been earmarked for strengthening the squad.
"We believe we have arguably one of the best playing squads in Europe and we are not entering a phase of substantial incremental investment," Corbidge said.
But he said the board would listen if the team management was convinced of the need to buy players and added that money would not be "frittered away" on non-football activities.
Corbidge said Newcastle were one of the most popular clubs with television viewers and would be ideally placed to benefit from the introduction of pay-per-view coverage in the next few years.
"I think that pay-per-view will come but in the meantime we must maximise returns from our existing activities," he said.
NatWest Markets said the flotation proceeds would be used to re-capitalise the club and provide a strong basis for future growth.
Newcastle are planning to move to a new 65 million stg stadium but Corbidge said the flotation would not directly fund the move.
"This will give us a solid platform and a whole variety of options to fund the stadium development," he said.
